\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of the configuration bound]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.configBound_mono}
\label{Complexity.Codec.configBound_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$n,s,s'$ be natural numbers. If $s\le s'$, then the configuration bound for input length
$n$ and space parameter $s$ is at most the configuration bound for input length $n$ and
space parameter $s'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Encoded step relation]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.StepRel}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002,

}
\label{Complexity.Codec.StepRel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$
be a Boolean string, and let $s,a,b$ be natural numbers. The encoded tuple consisting of
$x$ and the binary expansions of $a,b,s$ belongs to the step language of $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[A code path implies acceptance]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath}
\label{Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.Cfg.inWindow_init, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_of_acceptsWithin, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $L$ be a
language of Boolean strings, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume that $N$
decides $L$ in space $sp$. For a Boolean string $x$ and natural numbers $s,u,v$, suppose
$u$ is the code of the initial configuration on $x$ within window $s$, there is a finite
sequence of zero or more valid one-step transitions within that window from the
configuration coded by $u$ to the one coded by $v$, and $v$ is the code of a halted
configuration with output exactly $[1]$ within that window. Then $x\in L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership characterized by a code chain]
\lean{Complexity.Codec.mem_iff_codeChain}
\label{Complexity.Codec.mem_iff_codeChain}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt, Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.Codec.configBound_mono, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath, Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang, Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt, Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_inWindow, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $L$ be a
language of Boolean strings, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume that for every
input $x$, the machine halts after some common number $T$ of steps on every choice
string of length $T$, uses at most $sp(|x|)$ work-tape cells on every such run, and
accepts exactly the inputs in $L$. For any Boolean string $x$ and natural number $s$
with $sp(|x|)\le s$, we have $x\in L$ if and only if there are a natural number $t$ and
a sequence of natural numbers $(c_i)_{i\ge0}$ such that $t\le
3((|Q|+1)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k)$, the code $c_0$ describes the initial
configuration of $N$ on $x$ within window $s$, each consecutive pair $c_i,c_{i+1}$ for
$i<t$ describes a valid one-step transition between configurations within that window,
the code $c_t$ describes a halted accepting configuration within that window, and
$c_i<2^{(2W+2)(s+\log_2(|x|)+2)}$ for every $i\le t$. Here $k$ is the number of work
tapes, $Q$ is the finite state set, and $W$ is the codec's fixed chunk width for $N$.
\end{theorem}
